intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SMO gene.

paragraphs.text: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is a developmental disorder with a broad range of features. These can include hypothalamic hamartoma and microcephaly, atrioventricular septal defect, skeletal anomalies such as postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of the long bones, and aganglionosis of the enteric nervous system (Le et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) proposed the name 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS) for a possibly familial entity of congenital hypothalamic hamartoma with skeletal dysplasia and orofacial abnormalities.

checks.claim: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) proposed the name 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS) for a possibly familial entity of congenital hypothalamic hamartoma with skeletal dysplasia and orofacial abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings prompt us to consider skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities as common denominator and minimum criteria required to define a nosologically distinct, possibly familial entity, which we suggest calling "congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome" (CHHS).
checks.explanation: The abstract states both the proposed name and the defining criteria.

checks.explanation: The title says the paper reports two cases of hypothalamic hamartoma with associated developmental defects.

paragraphs.text: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) found congenital hypothalamic hamartomas at autopsy in 3 unrelated fetuses. In the first 2 fetuses, the tumor occurred with skeletal dysplasia only. In the third fetus, it was part of a nonrandom pattern of congenital malformations that suggested Meckel syndrome. In 1 family, a previous boy had died soon after birth with similar craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities. After analyzing reported cases of Pallister-Hall syndrome, the authors found that only skeletal dysplasia and orofacial abnormalities were constantly present. They proposed these as the minimum criteria for a distinct, possibly familial entity, which they called 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS).

paragraphs.text: Le et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the SMO gene in 7 individuals with PHLS from 5 independent families. Ciliogenesis was normal in cells from affected individuals, but hedgehog signal transduction was severely altered. This resulted either from altered trafficking through the primary cilium or from abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO. These cells also accumulated GLI2 at the tip of the primary cilium independently of hedgehog signaling. The authors suggested that SMO may help regulate basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.

paragraphs.text: Craig et al. (2008) studied 55 patients with sporadic, nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma and intractable epilepsy, comparing peripheral blood with surgically resected hamartoma tissue. They found no causative germline GLI3 mutations. However, 8 of the 55 (15%) resected tissue samples had somatic chromosomal abnormalities that included the GLI3 locus. These comprised a somatic abnormality on chromosome 7p in 1 sample and loss of heterozygosity within or around GLI3 in 8 patients. The somatic changes appeared to be highly variable.

checks.claim: Craig et al. (2008) studied 55 patients with sporadic, nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma and intractable epilepsy.
checks.evidence_quote: We isolated genomic DNA from peripheral blood and surgically resected HH tissue in 55 patients with sporadic HH and intractable epilepsy.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes 55 patients with sporadic HH and intractable epilepsy, and its conclusion calls them sporadic, nonsyndromic patients.

checks.claim: Craig et al. (2008) compared peripheral blood with surgically resected hamartoma tissue from patients with sporadic nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome-wide screen for loss of heterozygosity (LOH) and chromosomal abnormalities was performed with parallel analysis of blood and HH tissue with Affymetrix 10K SNP microarrays.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that blood and HH tissue from the same patients were analyzed side by side.

checks.claim: Craig et al. (2008) found no causative germline GLI3 mutations in 55 patients with sporadic nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma.
checks.evidence_quote: Resequencing of GLI3 did not identify causative germline mutations but did identify LOH within the GLI3 gene in the HH tissue samples of three patients.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that resequencing found no causative germline GLI3 mutations in the study cohort.

checks.claim: In the Craig et al. (2008) study, 8 of 55 (15%) resected hypothalamic hamartoma tissue samples had somatic chromosomal abnormalities that included the GLI3 locus.

checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same count and percentage, 8 of 55 (15%).

checks.claim: In the Craig et al. (2008) study, 1 resected hypothalamic hamartoma sample had a somatic abnormality on chromosome 7p.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a somatic chromosomal abnormality on chromosome 7p in one HH tissue sample.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a somatic 7p abnormality in one HH tissue sample.

checks.claim: In the Craig et al. (2008) study, 8 patients had loss of heterozygosity within or around GLI3 in resected hypothalamic hamartoma tissue.
checks.evidence_quote: did identify LOH within the GLI3 gene in the HH tissue samples of three patients. Further genotyping of 28 SNPs within and surrounding GLI3 identified five additional patients exhibiting LOH.
checks.explanation: Three patients plus five additional patients gives 8 with LOH within or around GLI3. These 8 match the overall total of 8 of 55, so the 7p case is probably among them rather than an extra case.

checks.claim: The somatic changes involving GLI3 in hypothalamic hamartoma tissue appeared to be highly variable.
checks.evidence_quote: These somatic mutations appear to be highly variable.
